desc:
Each interval [a, b] is a closed range with a < b. Interval [a, b] is covered by interval [c, d] when c ≤ a and b ≤ d, that is, it lies completely inside the other one.

All intervals in the list are pairwise different. Return how many intervals are not covered by any other interval of the list.

intervals = [[1, 4], [3, 6], [2, 8]]  ->  2

[3, 6] lies inside [2, 8]; the other two are not covered by anything.
constraints: All intervals are distinct as pairs [a, b]
hints: Checking every pair is O(n<sup>2</sup>). Can an ordering of the intervals remove the need to compare all pairs?
Sort by start ascending, and for equal starts by end descending. After that, any interval that could cover the current one comes earlier in the list.
Walk through the sorted list while keeping the largest end seen so far. The current interval is covered exactly when its end does not exceed that maximum.
editorial: After sorting by start ascending (ties: end descending), every interval that could cover interval i has start ≤ start[i], and if the starts are equal it has a larger end, so it appears before i. Therefore interval i is covered if and only if some earlier interval has end ≥ end[i], which is the same as saying the running maximum end is ≥ end[i].

So one pass is enough: if end > max_end, the interval is uncovered, count it, and update the maximum. Without the tie-break, two intervals with the same start and different ends would be handled in the wrong order. Time is O(n log n) for the sort, extra space O(n) for the sorted copy.
